ledger.note: By 538 Chu holds Zhongli. The page dates the Chu conquest only to 'sometime in the 6th century BC' and says that in 538 BC a Chu official fortified the city; 538 is the first year the pages show it Chu's. (Zhongli may have been a vassal of Wu from 576, when it hosted an interstate meeting where Wu negotiated for the first time.)

wars.outcome: Chu conquered Zhongli in the 6th century BC, held it by 538 BC and fortified it; the Wu king Liao took the city twenty years later (c. 518, the researcher's arithmetic) and Chu recovered it after Wu fell to Yue.
wars.note: The years are the page's loose chronology; the zone is the whole state. No contest event is written because the page dates no campaign.

certainty.note: No Zhongli boundary is on the page; soft throughout.
